findings.paper_title: County Council Budget Quarter 1 Monitoring Report 2026-27
findings.headline: Projected funding gap of £17.3m to £23.3m for 2027-28 will require significant service reductions
findings.detail: The approved MTFP projects a funding gap of £17.3m in 2027-28 under the most likely scenario. High-level modelling suggests an additional £6.0m pressure from higher inflation assumptions. The council has identified that "some of our services are costing substantially more than those services provided by other local authorities or what WG deem we should be spending", implying major service reviews are needed.
findings.matters: A £17.3m–£23.3m gap (5–7% of budget) cannot be closed through minor efficiencies. The council will be forced to make material changes to service scope or scale, which is typically a multi-year challenge and affects financial resilience.
findings.figures: Approved MTFP gap £17.3m in 2027-28, potential additional pressure £6.0m due to inflation
findings.quote: The approved MTFP 2026-27 to 2028-29 currently projects funding gap of £17.3m in 2027-28 (most likely scenario)" and "This has led to a potential increase in the projected funding gap of up to £6.0m" and "some of our services are costing substantially more than those services provided by other local authorities or what WG deem we should be spending, therefore, these services will require detailed review over the coming months"

findings.paper_title: County Council Budget Quarter 1 Monitoring Report 2026-27
findings.headline: Council Tax arrears have grown by £7m in one year with new regulations likely to worsen collection
findings.detail: Prior year arrears increased from £12.506m (31 March 2025) to £19.479m (31 March 2026). New collection regulations effective from April 2026 allow up to 12 reminders per year (vs. 3 previously) and extend the period before summons, with the report noting "the delay in recovery is likely to have an impact on the collection rate as the year progresses". A further £2.9m is under appeal with the Valuation Office, which has a 12-month backlog.
findings.matters: Council tax is a material income source; the 55% increase in arrears year-on-year combined with regulatory delays to recovery creates a sustained revenue risk. The Valuation Office backlog means this risk will persist for at least 12 months.
findings.figures: Arrears £19.479m (31 March 2026) vs £12.506m (31 March 2025), increase of £6.973m. £2.9m under appeal with Valuation Office (12-month backlog)
findings.quote: Council Tax Prior Year Arrears... 31 Mar 25 £m 12.506... 31 Mar 26 £m 19.479" and "the delay in recovery is likely to have an impact on the collection rate as the year progresses" and "At Q1, £2.9m of Council Tax arrears (including balances due for the 2026-27 financial year) is specifically linked to self-catering properties that have moved from NDR to Council Tax and are currently under appeal with the Valuation Office, with the intention of reverting back to NDR."

findings.paper_title: County Council Budget Quarter 1 Monitoring Report 2026-27
findings.headline: Adult social care costs escalating due to shift toward more complex, higher-cost care packages
findings.detail: Homecare is projecting a £1.292m overspend driven by increased volume of clients and higher care needs. The report explicitly notes a continuing trend of "shift toward more complex, higher-cost care packages" with "rising pressures expected in the medium to long term". Average homecare cost per hour has risen from £24.06 (2021-22) to £35.42 (2026-27 projection).
findings.matters: This represents a structural cost escalation in a major service area. The identified trend is expected to persist into the medium and long term, creating ongoing budget pressure with limited intervention levers.
findings.figures: Homecare overspend £1.292m, external homecare hours projected 364,105 (up from 334,331 in 2021-22), average cost per hour £35.42 (up from £24.06)
findings.quote: Homecare is projecting a £1.292m overspend... Overall trends continue to indicate a shift toward higher-cost care packages, with rising pressures expected in the medium to long term.

findings.paper_title: County Council Budget Quarter 1 Monitoring Report 2026-27
findings.headline: School ALN budget significantly overspent with uncertain Welsh Government funding
findings.detail: Additional Learning Needs spending is £1.166m over budget at Q1, with 388 pupils requiring support against 265 originally budgeted. The council is anticipating funding from Welsh Government to address this, but the WG's proposed £40m allocation was voted down and no additional funding can be assumed until revised budget proposals are published in November 2026.
findings.matters: This is a material unfunded pressure dependent on discretionary Welsh Government allocation that has already failed to secure approval once. The uncertainty affects the council's ability to balance the 2026-27 budget.
findings.figures: £1.166m overspend, 388 pupils requiring support vs 265 budgeted, £2.452m budget vs £3.618m needed
findings.quote: The demand and complexity of need within School ALN has resulted in an increase above budgeted levels during the first quarter of 2026-27. Projections include the assumption that this will continue throughout 2026-27 resulting in a £1.166m overspend in this area, albeit we anticipate that specific funding for ALN will be forthcoming from Welsh Government during 2026-27 to address this.

findings.paper_title: Corporate and Financial Planning Timetable and Budget Strategy for 2027-28 and beyond
findings.headline: Reserves positioned as contingency to fund ongoing operations if savings do not materialise
findings.detail: Budget strategy principle 29 states there is no planned use of reserves to fund the base budget, but flexibility is available to use them if required. Given the £17.3m gap and aggressive savings targets, this signals reserves are viewed as fallback if cuts cannot be delivered.
findings.matters: A council contemplating reserve drawdown to fund ongoing operations signals the expenditure base is unsustainable; reserve depletion masks rather than solves the structural deficit
findings.quote: No planned use of earmarked reserves or the general fund working balance to fund the core base revenue budget, but flexibility available to utilise them if required.
